methods.returns: { policy, combatOnScene, allowed, reason, wish, ghost, ownedOnTop, patched: { drag, keyboard }, sceneId, version, settings: { <key>: scope }, combatExempt: string[], group: { enabled, fight, patched: { drop, click }, regime, limits, groups, last, fallbacks, stopped, cut, step, undo, told, pending, wave, flushed, queue, leading, perf }, stop: { last }, assist: { tripped }, migrated }
methods.doc: Why ghost is or isn't on for this client on a scene (opts.sceneId, default the viewed one): the GM policy, whether a combat there stops ghosting, this client's button (wish), whether the two core methods are wrapped, every setting key with its scope (ghost and ownedOnTop are client settings), and combatExempt: the ids of your tokens there that may ghost through the fight (incorporeal feat or the GM's flag; [] when no fight blocks). group (0.4.0; 0.9.0 the drop): drag help on this client — enabled (groupDrags), fight (groupDrags: a group drag in a fight is the fight file, one member at a time), whether the drop and click wraps are in, the regime of your controlled tokens (combat when one is in a started combat, else free), the limits (maxMembers: 24 since 0.10), how many groups this client holds (a click on one member stops them all), the last drop (mode, reason, result, ms, async, stacked; 0.10 a group's shape: march / swarm, leader, target, stayed: the ids named, waves, plan: { timingMs, searches, failed, total: the last start, pack: the pack's start (one wave after the leader, or once a leader that starts behind is a wave past the frontmost member), members, crowded, staggerMs }) and the last few reasons a drop went to core; stopped: the last stop of a group (late: members whose wave was on its way, stopped when their move came back; lateTotal); cut: the last wall raised or door shut that stopped moves this client drives (out of combat, where drawn); step (0.8.3): the last next square of a move this client drove that it did not send (why: wall, standing, unrendered, wallUnrendered); undo (0.8.3): the last move whose undo entries were merged into one; told (0.9.0): the last notices this client showed (kind, reason, text); pending (0.9.0): the file's waves this client still has to send ([{ gid, at, ids }]); wave: the last later wave it sent (members, sent, skipped: no longer at their start, shut: a wall across their way, undrawn: no longer drawn here, named); flushed: the last time this tab went to the background with waves to send (members; 0.10 L3: kept, on their own timers, and retimed, due past 3 s and timed for 3 s); queue: the last fight queue (members, order: the leader, then least walk left (0.10 L3), sent, stayed, there: the ids already on their square, skipped, watchdog, walks (0.10 L3): each member's walk [{ id, planned, sent: squares, left: the movement it had left (dnd5e's speed less this turn's movement history; null: no usable speed, the whole way), why: speed when it stopped where its movement ran out, inside: paid squares past its stop inside a member }], ended: done / click / turn / deleted / stopped / noRoute, running; 0.10 a new drop no longer ends it); leading (0.10): the ids drawn on top now, each the leader of a group drag still walking (its move's pentarynMovementLead); perf: drops handled, the last and longest (ms). stop.last (0.4.11): this client's last click-stop (tokenId, name, how, via: click / board / door / api, members, whole, pastDoor, walkedOn: members it could not stop clear of a token at rest, which walked on to their own squares), or null. assist.tripped (0.8.0): the circuit breaker's trip on this client ({ at, why }) or null; migrated: what migrateSettings carried over at ready.

Nothing moves. Needs a drawn canvas (a browser tab, not the headless GM). NOT_FOUND / BAD_ARGS / NO_CANVAS as a refusal object.

sideEffects: the token's pending movement (stopMovement, in combat)
methods.doc: Stop a moving token as a click on it would: out of combat it is put where it is drawn; in a started combat the client that started the move stops it at the next square (stopMovement). A GM asks that client directly (the pentaryn-movement.stopOwn query: GM sender only), so a GM may stop any move; a player asks the active GM through this row's relay, which stops it only when it started the move and the sender owns the token (NOT_INITIATOR / NOT_OWNER otherwise). Stopping a member of a group stops the whole group: on the client that sent it every member, its unsent waves and its fight queue; elsewhere this one, and the dragger's screen stops the rest. Never held back by the 400 ms arming a click waits for. NOT_MOVING when it is not moving or you cannot control it.

Live smoke checks after a sync: published, settings readable, the core methods wrapped (drag, keyboard, pathfinding, group drop, click to stop), hooks registered.

settings.doc: GM policy for player ghost movement: off, exploration (off while a combat runs on the scene) or always.
The mode the GM toolbar button restores when it is switched back on (exploration or always).
This player's ghost button (their wish); in effect only while the policy allows it. Client scope.
Draw this player's own tokens on top, on their screen only. Client scope.
Tier A, drag pathfinding round walls and standing tokens (with the ruler and a single token's click-stop): everyone (default), gm (GM drags only) or off. Read live on every drag.
This client's drags find a path (when the world setting allows it). Client scope. Corners are always rounded where that costs nothing (0.8.0 folded smoothCorners in).

Group drags (0.8.0; was groupMovement): the token grabbed leads (0.10): dropped on the floor a march (the leader on the drop square, the rest behind it), on a visible token outside the group a swarm round it; out of combat the leader at once and the rest a wave later as one pack, single file only at a narrow point, the last within 4 s (0.10 L2); in a fight the leader first, then one member at a time, each a single move whose square is picked and routed at its turn (0.9.0, replaces tier C). Up to 24 tokens (0.10). Off: core's move, cut before standing tokens.

The table's drag help (0.4.9): off, every drag is plain Foundry dragging (no pathfinding, no group plan, no single-drop routing); the GM's toolbar button flips it. Pathfinding and the tier gates keep their own values. The circuit breaker (0.8.0) switches it off after repeated failures.
